name: dns
description: The name layer of the mod protocol. Derives a zone from the module fleet — one name per routed module plus the apex, the wildcard and the nameservers — serves it authoritatively over UDP and TCP, and publishes what the protocol attributes each module to (the owner address it declares, its schema CID, and the key this box signs its module cards with) as _mod TXT records beside the address the name resolves to. Resolves a module name, a hostname, a gateway path or a whole URL into the app, API and MCP addresses behind it, checks what it holds against what a public resolver actually returns, and tells anyone who asks how to run the protocol on a host of their own. Reads are open; every change is attributed to a signed mod-protocol address, with the system zone reserved to the deployment owner and every other zone owned by whoever registered it. A REST API, a browser console, a CLI and 28 MCP tools run the same functions on one port.
backend: api.py — python stdlib only (http.server + socketserver); the DNS wire format is implemented in-tree in wire.py
frontend: console.html — served at /dns on the API port, so the console and the API are same-origin. An 8-bit console: Press Start 2P and VT323 self-hosted from /dns/fonts, a drawn pixel sprite instead of an icon font, hard-edged panels and a CRT overlay you can switch off. Seven tabs — RESOLVE, ATTRIBUTION, ZONE, FLEET, YOUR HOST, MCP, OPERATIONS — where MCP handshakes this module's own endpoint and calls its tools from the browser. Sign-in is the wallet: MetaMask personal_signs the mod-protocol token in the browser, no transaction and no gas. The layout is one column, centred and capped: the readings and the tabs each stay one scrolling line as the screen narrows, and the guide dock insets the whole page rather than covering the header it points at.

engine.wire.py: DNS on the wire — message parse/build, every record type this server writes, and a stub resolver for asking the public internet
engine.fleet.py: the module fleet as a name space: which modules declared route:true, their ports, and the fields the protocol attributes them by
engine.attrib.py: attribution — owner, schema CID and the box key, published as _mod TXT records and checkable against the protocol's signed module card
engine.zone.py: zones: the derived layer computed from the fleet, the stored layer somebody wrote, and who may write which
engine.server.py: the authoritative listener — UDP and TCP, wildcards, CNAME chasing, NODATA vs NXDOMAIN
engine.resolver.py: a mod name in, every address out; the diff against what a public resolver returns; the plan for running the protocol on your own host
engine.identity.py: who is calling — one mod-protocol token, three standings (owner, holder, anon)
engine.ops.py: the operation catalog and the append-only change log
engine.guide.py: the guide — the beginner surface: a setup checklist scored against the live box, a glossary that says what each word points at here, and plain-word questions matched to hand-written answers grounded in a real lookup. No model
engine.actions.py: the operations themselves — the REST API, the MCP tools and the CLI all call these

attribution.format: v=mod1 mod=<name> owner=<address> key=<box address> cid=<schema CID> ver=<version> orbit=<core|orbit> app=/<mod> api=/api/<mod>
attribution.owner: what the module declares in its own config.json — a module that declares none publishes none
attribution.key: the address this deployment signs its module cards with; m.info(<mod>) returns the signed card and m.verify_info checks it

derives.@: SOA, NS and the A record for the box the zone points at
derives.*: the wildcard, so a new module needs no DNS change
derives.{mod}: one A record per routed module in the fleet
derives._mod.{mod}: who that module is attributed to
derives._mod-challenge: the TXT token that proves a zone is delegated here

health.docs: Liveness — host, zone count, listener state

overview.docs: The whole naming picture in one object

resolve.docs: query= — a module name, hostname, gateway path or URL → every address for it

attribution.docs: name=, verify= — who a module is attributed to: owner, schema CID, and the signed module card

lookup.docs: name=, type= — what this name server would answer

check.docs: name=, type= — held here vs what a public resolver returns

plan.docs: host=, target= — how to run the protocol on a host you control

modules.docs: The routed fleet as a name space

zones.docs: Every zone served here and who owns each

zone_register.docs: Register a domain you control — you own every record in it

records.docs: Merged records — stored, plus what the protocol derives

record_set.docs: Write one record into a zone you own

record_delete.docs: name=, type=, value= — delete one stored record

zone_target.docs: Point a zone's apex, wildcard and module names at one address

zone_verify.docs: Look for the challenge TXT in the public DNS

operations.docs: The catalog — every operation and the standing it requires

ops.docs: The change log — every mutation and the address behind it

whoami.docs: Your standing and what you can run

guide.docs: The beginner surface: an ordered checklist marked against this deployment, the glossary and worked prompts

guide_ask.docs: question= — plain words in, an answer grounded in what this box is doing; no model, and it says when it does not know

guide_term.docs: word= — one piece of DNS vocabulary, with what it means here

router_sync.docs: OWNER — hand the host to the caddy module so HTTP and DNS agree

mcp.docs: MCP JSON-RPC 2.0 (Streamable HTTP) — 28 tools, same handlers as the REST routes

transports.stdio: python3 mcp.py — runs as this box's own identity

mcp.auth: the caller's mod-protocol token as Authorization: Bearer; every read tool needs none

standings.owner: the deployment owner — the system zone (the protocol host itself), the settings, the listener and the router sync. Claimed by the first signed caller.
standings.holder: any signed caller — registers and fully owns their own host and every record in it, with no permission needed from the owner
standings.anon: reads everything: zones, records, the resolver, the change log. Changes nothing.

env.DNS_DIR: state dir: settings, zones, owner, change log (default ~/.mod/dns)
env.DNS_ROOTS: colon-separated module roots to derive names from (default /root/mod/mod/orbit:/root/mod/mod/core)
env.DNS_OWNER: fallback owner address when ~/.mod/dns/owner.json is absent
env.DNS_OPEN: 1 = collapse every caller into one local identity (local development only)
env.DNS_TOKEN_MAX_AGE: seconds a mod-protocol token stays valid (default 7 days)
env.DNS_TOKEN: token the stdio MCP transport signs its calls with

legacy: mod-dns/ (Rust + libp2p) and app/ (Next.js) are the retired first prototype, kept for reference; nothing in the module calls them
